fidelityPolicy.note: A3 formalizes M16 conformance semantics. It does not make HYBRID or ASSESSMENT invariants machine-decidable.

invariantFamilies.name: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning

assessmentModes.meaning: Material portions can be checked from declared architecture structure, identifiers, mappings or versioned configuration.
assessmentModes.typicalEvidence: Architecture registry, mapping graph/table, declared lifecycle/profile structure, identifier/version checks.
assessmentModes.automationCeiling: May support decisive machine checks only for conditions fully represented by the formal artifacts; does not prove runtime correctness or assurance.

assessmentModes.meaning: Structural checks are useful but sufficient assessment also requires interpretation of authority, semantics, behavior, evidence or context.
assessmentModes.typicalEvidence: Structural evidence plus architecture review, contract evidence, policy/currentness evidence, runtime samples.
assessmentModes.automationCeiling: Machine checks may support assessment; accountable review is required for final satisfaction.

assessmentModes.meaning: Accountable judgement is primary; machine checks can support but cannot safely determine the conclusion by themselves.
assessmentModes.typicalEvidence: Architecture rationale, assurance review, contextual trust/fitness assessment, governance judgement.
assessmentModes.automationCeiling: Machine support only; final satisfaction cannot be asserted automatically.

applicabilityStates.meaning: The invariant architectural condition materially arises within the assessed subject/scope.
The condition genuinely does not arise in the bounded scope and that conclusion is justified.
During assessment, applicability itself cannot yet be established.

invariantResults.meaning: The applicable invariant has sufficient evidence to establish satisfaction.
The applicable invariant is demonstrably violated.
Available evidence cannot establish satisfaction or violation with the confidence required by the invariant.
The invariant condition genuinely does not arise in the bounded scope and the rationale is justified.

conformanceSubjectClasses.name: Enterprise HDIP Architecture
conformanceSubjectClasses.meaning: Enterprise-wide or multi-domain HDIP target/current architecture.

conformanceSubjectClasses.name: Domain / Portfolio HDIP Architecture
conformanceSubjectClasses.meaning: A Data, Information, Intelligence or cross-domain bounded architecture.

conformanceSubjectClasses.name: Platform / Solution Architecture
conformanceSubjectClasses.meaning: A bounded platform, solution or capability architecture claiming HDIP alignment.

conformanceSubjectClasses.name: Product / Capability Realization Architecture
conformanceSubjectClasses.meaning: A bounded Product or non-Product capability realization using applicable PDEP/SSCF/runtime responsibilities.

conformanceSubjectClasses.name: Concrete Realization Mapping
conformanceSubjectClasses.meaning: The mapping from canonical/Profile architecture into actual deployed/human/provider Realization Units.

claimTypes.name: Core Architecture Conformance
claimTypes.meaning: The subject preserves all applicable M16 core invariants and the applicable responsibilities/contracts of the HDIP-CLA 0.1 baseline.

claimTypes.name: Profile Conformance
claimTypes.meaning: The subject is Core-conformant and satisfies a named, governed, M16-valid HDIP Profile.

claimTypes.name: Realization Mapping Conformance
claimTypes.meaning: A concrete implementation mapping faithfully realizes the claimed Core/Profile architecture, including traceability to Realization Units, M12 contracts, M13 boundaries/EBCs, evidence responsibilities, currentness and failure/recovery obligations.

overallOutcomes.meaning: Every applicable core invariant is SATISFIED; N/A results have justified scope rationale; all obligations required by the claim type are satisfied.
At least one applicable core invariant is VIOLATED, or a mandatory claim-type obligation is demonstrably violated.
No applicable core invariant is known to be violated, but one or more material applicable obligations cannot be determined with sufficient evidence.

evidencePackage.name: Subject identity/version
evidencePackage.minimumContent: Stable subject ID and assessed version.

evidencePackage.name: Scope / architecture boundary
evidencePackage.minimumContent: Organizational, solution, Product/capability and logical boundary.

evidencePackage.name: External authority map
evidencePackage.minimumContent: GEDRM/GEARM/GEAIRM, BPS/PIN, Product-family, policy/legal, Decision/action and other authorities relied upon.

evidencePackage.name: ABB / responsibility mapping
evidencePackage.minimumContent: Canonical/specialized ABB and embedded responsibility realization.

evidencePackage.name: Registry / projection / compilation map
evidencePackage.minimumContent: Applicable M09 Registries, HPD/RRG/SYNCTX/RGB/Realization Plan/Blueprint Binding/Compilation Record responsibilities.

evidencePackage.name: Interaction Contract map
evidencePackage.minimumContent: Material M12 interactions and contract obligations.

evidencePackage.name: External Boundary map
evidencePackage.minimumContent: Material M13 Boundary Families, Boundary Instances and EBCs.

evidencePackage.name: Realization / Profile map
evidencePackage.minimumContent: M14 Realization Pattern(s), Realization Units and Profile obligations.

evidencePackage.name: Version/currentness/historical state
evidencePackage.minimumContent: Material versions, effective/currentness state and assessment time.

evidencePackage.name: Invariant assessment record
evidencePackage.minimumContent: Applicability, mode, result, rationale and evidence references for M16-I01..I48.

evidencePackage.name: Limitations / N/A / unresolved evidence
evidencePackage.minimumContent: Explicit gaps, N/A rationale, indeterminate conditions and unresolved dependencies.

evidencePackage.name: Accountability / retention
evidencePackage.minimumContent: Accountable assessor/authority, assessment version/time and retained evidence location/reference.

profileOperations.meaning: Select an applicable baseline option or pattern.
Make an optional/conditional baseline responsibility mandatory within Profile scope.
Strengthen a threshold, control, evidence or lifecycle obligation.
Bind a baseline concept to a bounded enterprise/domain context without redefining it.
Introduce a family/domain specialization consistent with the parent authority.
Reduce allowed choices or topology/interaction options for a bounded risk/context reason.
Add local obligations/fields/controls that do not conflict with core meaning.
Require stronger/additional evidence, assurance or human review.
Constrain permitted M14 patterns/localities/providers for the bounded Profile.
Reduce an applicable core invariant or mandatory baseline obligation.
Waive a violation and still report Profile/Core conformance.
Take ownership of GEDRM/GEARM/GEAIRM or other external semantics.
Redefine BPS/PIN Product qualification or Product Intrinsic Nature.
Infer Data, Product, policy or Decision authority from platform participation.
Erase Data/Information/AI Product-family distinctions.
Impose a Data-, Information- or Intelligence-specific lifecycle/construct on all families without authority/evidence.
Suppress an applicable X1-X9 obligation because implementation is inconvenient.
Eliminate material evidence/currentness/history requirements needed by the parent baseline.
Silently rename/redefine P1-P5, X1-X9, ABBs or M12/M13 identities as different architecture semantics.
Erase their canonical responsibility distinction.
Create Product status from registration, publication, deployment, exposure or repeated use.
Project latest Profile/policy/topology state backwards onto earlier occurrences.
Mark a material core obligation not applicable merely to avoid remediation.

realizationMappingMinimum: Realization Unit(s) / human process / adjacent system

safelyAutomatable: selected lifecycle stage/projection synchronization where mechanically represented
evidence-reference presence and staleness flags where time semantics are explicit
hybrid: whether a local semantic extension has captured external authority
whether two implementations truly preserve Product-family distinction
whether compilation has manufactured a relationship from weak evidence
whether an Access Decision has leaked into consequential-action authority
whether a provider substitution is semantically/contractually safe
whether historical reconstruction is materially sufficient
assessmentOnly: architecture significance of a semantic/authority gap
whether a complex realization introduces unacceptable hidden authority or evidence coupling

assessmentWorkflow: Identify Conformance Subject, version, scope and claim type.
Identify HDIP-CLA baseline and applicable concrete Profile(s).
Determine applicable P1-P5 responsibilities and X1-X9 Overlays.
Trace canonical/specialized ABB and embedded responsibility realization.
Identify PDEP / SSCF / CEP lifecycle/experience applicability.
Identify material M13 Boundary Families / EBCs.
Record M14 Realization Pattern(s), Profile(s) and Realization Mapping.
Select the smallest useful M15 Reference View/Flow set for review.
Gather STRUCTURAL, HYBRID and ASSESSMENT evidence.
Record invariant results with rationale/evidence references.
Determine overall outcome: CONFORMANT / NONCONFORMANT / INDETERMINATE.
Record accountable assessor/authority, assessment version and time.
Preserve the Conformance Evidence Package for historical reconstruction.
Define change triggers that require scoped reassessment.

invariants.name: Semantic authority preservation
invariants.canonicalCondition: HDIP-CLA SHALL NOT incompatibly redefine concepts, relationships or invariants owned by GEDRM, GEARM, GEAIRM or other applicable semantic authorities.

invariants.name: Product authority preservation
invariants.canonicalCondition: Generic Product identity, Product Intrinsic Nature and Product qualification SHALL remain governed by BPS/PIN rather than inferred by HDIP.

invariants.name: Product-family authority preservation
invariants.canonicalCondition: Data Product, Information Product, AI Product and other Product-family qualification/classification SHALL remain with the applicable Product-family authority.

invariants.name: Scoped authority
invariants.canonicalCondition: Authority used by HDIP SHALL be explicit for an applicable scope, role, purpose, lifecycle state and/or jurisdiction where those distinctions matter; platform participation SHALL NOT imply universal authority.

invariants.name: Shared-realization non-transfer
invariants.canonicalCondition: Co-location, shared storage, shared runtime, shared registry, shared UI or shared platform realization SHALL NOT by itself transfer semantic, Product, policy, decision or ownership authority.

invariants.name: Semantic-gap escalation
invariants.canonicalCondition: Where HDIP needs a semantic concept not owned by HDIP, the gap SHALL be referred to or extended through the appropriate semantic authority rather than silently minted as platform semantics.

invariants.name: Authority non-transitivity
invariants.canonicalCondition: Authority, approval, entitlement, policy applicability or ownership SHALL NOT become automatically transitive merely because a dependency, composition or interaction crosses an HDIP boundary.

invariants.name: Responsibility before component
invariants.canonicalCondition: A canonical HDIP ABB or mandatory implementation responsibility SHALL be justified by explicit architectural responsibility; a noun, tool, service label or historical box alone is insufficient.

invariants.name: Logical plane semantics
invariants.canonicalCondition: A future HDIP Plane SHALL represent a coherent logical responsibility grouping and SHALL NOT imply a mandatory system, deployment unit, network tier, team, organizational boundary or lifecycle step.

invariants.name: Topology independence
invariants.canonicalCondition: HDIP-CLA conformance SHALL NOT depend on centralized, federated, distributed, edge, embedded, provider-managed or hybrid deployment topology unless a narrower Profile explicitly requires it.

invariants.name: Many-to-many realization
invariants.canonicalCondition: One implementation MAY realize responsibilities from several HDIP logical structures, and one HDIP responsibility MAY be distributed across several implementations.

invariants.name: Source-plane non-equivalence
invariants.canonicalCondition: GEDRA, GEARA and GEAIRA plane numbering, placement or lexical similarity SHALL NOT force one-to-one HDIP plane mapping.

invariants.name: Cross-cutting visibility
invariants.canonicalCondition: A responsibility that is cross-cutting in an applicable source architecture SHALL NOT be silently localized into one future HDIP plane without explicit justification that preserves its cross-cutting obligations.

invariants.name: Foundation separation
invariants.canonicalCondition: Compute, storage, networking, messaging, identity infrastructure, orchestration and other utility capabilities SHALL NOT acquire semantic, Product, governance or domain authority merely because they enable those responsibilities.

invariants.name: Architecture traceability
invariants.canonicalCondition: Every future canonical HDIP Plane, Overlay, ABB and material interaction SHALL trace to upstream responsibilities, explicit enterprise platform requirements and/or justified HDIP-specific coordination responsibilities.

invariants.name: Domain distinction
invariants.family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
invariants.canonicalCondition: Data, Information and Intelligence SHALL remain distinguishable architectural/semantic concerns even where one platform capability co-realizes responsibilities from more than one domain.

invariants.name: No cross-domain inheritance
invariants.family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
invariants.canonicalCondition: A Data-specific, Information-specific or Intelligence-specific construct SHALL NOT automatically generalize to the other domains through shared implementation or naming similarity.

invariants.name: No automatic Productness
invariants.family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
invariants.canonicalCondition: Composition, generation, transformation, persistence, deployment, publication, registration, cataloguing, marketplace presence, API exposure, repeated use or consumption SHALL NOT by itself establish Product identity.

invariants.name: Product-family distinction
invariants.family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
invariants.canonicalCondition: Co-realization of Data Products, Information Products and AI Products SHALL NOT collapse them into one HDIP-local Product family or type.

invariants.name: Composition non-inheritance
invariants.family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
invariants.canonicalCondition: Using, depending on, containing, deriving from or invoking a Product/capability SHALL NOT by itself transfer its Product family, ontology type, ownership or authority to the dependent/composed result.

invariants.name: Direct capability validity
invariants.family: Data, Information, Intelligence and Product identity
invariants.canonicalCondition: HDIP SHALL be able to support governed Data, Information or Intelligence capability use where Product qualification is not intended; Productization SHALL NOT be a mandatory gateway for every governed interaction.

invariants.name: Governed self-service
invariants.canonicalCondition: Self-service SHALL operate inside applicable authority, policy, security, privacy, quality, evidence and lifecycle constraints; self-service SHALL NOT mean unrestricted infrastructure or data access.

invariants.name: Intent/compilation separation
invariants.canonicalCondition: Participant-declared intent, business semantics and accountable judgement SHALL remain distinguishable from platform resolution, compilation, provisioning and automation.

invariants.name: Automation non-ownership
invariants.canonicalCondition: HDIP automation SHALL NOT transfer Product ownership, Data authority, policy authority or decision accountability to the compiler/runtime merely because the platform performs most technical work.

invariants.name: Judgement honesty
invariants.canonicalCondition: Architecture/governance decisions requiring contextual or accountable judgement SHALL NOT be represented as machine-proven solely because metadata, telemetry, rules or model outputs exist.

invariants.name: PDEP canonical lifecycle identity
invariants.canonicalCondition: PDEP SHALL remain the canonical HDIP Product Development and Evolution Process identity; historical SSPD terminology MAY remain only for traceability and SHALL NOT become a competing lifecycle.

invariants.name: Progressive PDEP projection
invariants.canonicalCondition: PDEP G0 and PDEP Spec A MAY compress/group canonical stages for progressive disclosure, while PDEP Spec C SHALL remain synchronized with the canonical applicable detailed PDEP lifecycle.

invariants.name: Experience non-authority
invariants.canonicalCondition: Interactive flow players, diagrams, dashboards and experience projections SHALL NOT independently create lifecycle stages, authority, Product identity, ABBs or architecture semantics.

invariants.name: Projection non-authority
invariants.canonicalCondition: HPD, SYNCTX, resolved graphs, compiled governance bundles, compilation packs and similar HDIP-generated projections SHALL NOT override the authoritative semantics or governance sources they reference.

invariants.name: Compiler non-invention
invariants.canonicalCondition: HDIP resolution/compilation SHALL NOT manufacture semantic relationships, Product identity, policy authority, joinability, provenance, dependencies or obligations from weak evidence or naming similarity.

invariants.name: Logical registry independence
invariants.canonicalCondition: ADS, Product, Schema, Policy, Capability and Blueprint registry responsibilities SHALL remain logically distinguishable even where one implementation realizes several of them.

invariants.name: Registry non-qualification
invariants.canonicalCondition: Registration SHALL NOT by itself prove authoritative status, Product status, control effectiveness, semantic correctness, fitness or HDIP conformance.

invariants.name: Registry/catalog/marketplace distinction
invariants.canonicalCondition: Registry, Catalog and Marketplace responsibilities SHALL NOT be treated as architectural synonyms even when exposed through one user experience or implementation.

invariants.name: Shared registry realization allowed
invariants.canonicalCondition: HDIP MAY consolidate registry implementation where operationally useful provided logical identities, ownership, contracts, lifecycle and authority boundaries remain distinguishable.

invariants.name: Evidence by construction
invariants.family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
invariants.canonicalCondition: Material HDIP interactions SHOULD emit or retain applicable provenance, control, quality, observability and lifecycle evidence sufficient for later reconstruction and assessment.

invariants.name: Trust is contextual
invariants.family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
invariants.canonicalCondition: Platform location, certification label, popularity, centralization, Product status or registry presence SHALL NOT be treated as universal proof of trust or fitness; trust assessment SHALL remain contextual and evidence-based.

invariants.name: Missing evidence is not positive evidence
invariants.family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
invariants.canonicalCondition: Missing, stale, inaccessible or materially ambiguous evidence SHALL NOT be interpreted as positive assurance.

invariants.name: Version/currentness distinction
invariants.family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
invariants.canonicalCondition: Version identity, latest/newest status and governed currentness SHALL remain distinguishable; newest SHALL NOT automatically mean current or approved.

invariants.name: Historical truth
invariants.family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
invariants.canonicalCondition: Later supersession, revocation, re-evaluation, upstream change, rollback or re-publication SHALL NOT silently rewrite which semantics, Product Version, policy/control, dependency, context or realization governed a historical occurrence.

invariants.name: Provenance is not assurance
invariants.family: Evidence, trust, version and historical meaning
invariants.canonicalCondition: Provenance and lineage SHALL support traceability but SHALL NOT by themselves prove correctness, authorization, control effectiveness, assurance or Fitness for Use.

invariants.name: Canonical structure integrity
invariants.canonicalCondition: A conformant HDIP architecture SHALL preserve the canonical identity and responsibility meaning of P1-P5, X1-X9, HDIP-FND and the M08 ABB catalogue; implementation grouping, view projection or profile specialization SHALL NOT silently redefine those canonical structures.

invariants.name: Interaction-contract preservation
invariants.canonicalCondition: Material interactions SHALL preserve the applicable M12 Interaction Contract identity and obligations even when the participating responsibilities are co-located, embedded, distributed, provider-operated or implemented through a mechanism other than a network API.

invariants.name: External-boundary jurisdiction preservation
invariants.canonicalCondition: Material crossings of an M13 Boundary Family SHALL preserve the applicable external authority, jurisdiction, currentness, evidence and failure obligations; physical co-location or shared-provider realization SHALL NOT erase the logical boundary.

invariants.name: Product-access / consequence separation
invariants.canonicalCondition: Product or Product-Port access approval, entitlement or successful consumption SHALL NOT by itself authorize a downstream consequential Decision, Tool use, Digital Action or Physical Action where separate point-of-use authority is applicable.

invariants.name: Lifecycle / runtime non-equivalence
invariants.canonicalCondition: PDEP, SSCF and CEP SHALL remain lifecycle/experience compositions and SHALL NOT be interpreted as mandatory synchronous runtime pipelines; an established governed runtime MAY reuse current lifecycle state until material change requires re-evaluation.

invariants.name: Realization mapping traceability
invariants.canonicalCondition: A concrete realization claiming HDIP alignment SHALL retain traceability from applicable canonical responsibilities, ABBs, Interaction Contracts, Boundary Families and Profile obligations to the Realization Units, human processes or adjacent systems that satisfy them.

invariants.name: Adjacent-conformance independence
invariants.canonicalCondition: HDIP conformance SHALL NOT by itself establish conformance to GEDRA, GEARA, GEAIRA, BPS/PIN, a Product-family specification, an external standard or provider certification, and conformance to an adjacent specification SHALL NOT by itself establish HDIP conformance.

invariants.name: Profile monotonicity
invariants.canonicalCondition: An HDIP Profile MAY select, tighten, contextualize, specialize, narrow and extend the baseline for a bounded scope, but SHALL NOT weaken, waive or incompatibly redefine an applicable core invariant or transfer authority from an external semantic, Product, policy or Decision authority.
